A '''Hosaka plot''' is a [[Graphical model|graphical]] depiction used to evaluate the quality of a compressed image. A Hosaka plot shows  [[Image noise|noise level]]s at a number of scales.<ref>{{citation|title=Introduction to document image processing techniques|first=Ronald G.|last=Matteson|publisher=Artech House|year=1995|isbn=9780890064924|pages=244–246}}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Eskicioglu | first1 = A. M.
 | last2 = Fisher | first2 = P. S.
 | doi = 10.1109/26.477498
 | issue = 12
 | journal = IEEE Transactions on Communications
 | pages = 2959–2965
 | title = Image quality measures and their performance
 | volume = 43
 | year = 1995| hdl = 2060/19940023754| hdl-access = free
 }}.</ref> Hosoka plots are named after K. Hosoka, who wrote about them in 1986.<ref>{{citation|first=K.|last=Hosaka|contribution=A new picture quality evaluation method|title=Proceedings of Picture Coding Symposium, Tokyo, Japan|year=1986}}.</ref>
